## Summary

Fixes #103386.

`openclaw googlemeet leave <session-id>` on the Chrome transports printed `left <session-id>` and marked the session `ended`, but only ran the registered stop hook (the realtime audio bridge; in transcribe mode nothing at all). No code path touched the meeting, so the browser participant kept sitting in the call — a ghost participant receiving audio/captions after the operator was told it left. Twilio sessions already end the real call via their stop hook, so the transports were inconsistent.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/types.ts` + `chrome.ts`: join now persists the exact tab identity on the session — `browserTargetId` plus `browserTabOpenedByPlugin` (opened via `/tabs/open` vs adopted via `reuseExistingTab`). `openMeetWithBrowserRequest` returns it through both the local and node launch paths.
- `chrome.ts`: new `leaveChromeMeet` / `leaveChromeMeetOnNode` (shared `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest` core). Leave acts on the persisted target only: verifies the tab still exists (already-closed is a clean no-op), clicks Meet's **Leave call** button via browser evaluate (reliable now that tabs are pinned to `?hl=en`), then closes the tab **only when the plugin opened it** — reused user-owned tabs get the click but stay open. Failures degrade to session notes instead of throwing.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: `leave()` calls the browser leave for `chrome`/`chrome-node` sessions and records the outcome in session notes. Guards:
  - sessions with no tracked tab (e.g. `chrome.launch: false`, or browser control never returned a targetId) get an explicit note instead of a guessy URL match;
  - the internal tab-reassignment path in `join()` passes `keepBrowserTab: true` so agent handoff keeps the in-call tab and avoids lobby re-admission;
  - the shared-tab guard compares the persisted `browserTargetId` + node context — same meeting URL in a different browser/node no longer suppresses departure.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: `leave` row now documents the Chrome-transport behavior.

### Review follow-up (b95168f8ece)

All three ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed: leave no longer rediscovers tabs by URL (persisted `targetId` from join), never closes tabs it did not open (opened-vs-reused ownership tracked), and the shared-tab guard is scoped to the actual target + browser context. A reused-tab regression test now covers the default `reuseExistingTab: true` path end to end.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 209 tests passed. New/updated regressions: plugin-opened tab leave (click + close on the exact persisted target), reused user-owned tab leave (click, `DELETE` throws in the mock if attempted, tab stays open), already-closed tab leave (clean note, no `DELETE`), and a vm test that the leave script clicks only an enabled Leave call button.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- oxfmt / oxlint on touched files — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `googlemeet leave` leaves the browser participant in the Google Meet call on chrome/chrome-node transports while reporting `left`.
Real environment tested: No live Google Meet call was run; behavior is proven at the browser-proxy request boundary with the plugin's existing stubbed-gateway test harness (same harness the join/status paths use), covering opened, reused, and already-closed tab lifecycles.

What was not tested: A live Meet meeting (real Chrome, real Google account) and the chrome-node transport against a physical node; both share `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest`, which is covered by the harness. Live-call proof of actual participant departure is pending a real Meet setup.

target.title: fix(gateway): align runtime config activation with subsystem hot-reload publish (#103736)
target.body:
Closes #103736

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway config hot reload that changes hooks, cron, and channel settings simultaneously leaves the process in a mixed state for up to 5 minutes when a channel restart is deferred waiting for active work to drain. During that window, `getRuntimeConfig()` already returns the new configuration while hook routing still resolves against the old hooks config and cron RPCs still target the old (already stopped) cron instance.

This means a hook request arriving mid-window is routed to the wrong agent or session, and a cron job created or deleted in that window can be silently ineffective.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is that `onHotReload` commits the runtime config snapshot (`activate: true`) before calling `applyHotReload`, while `applyHotReload` only publishes hooks, cron, heartbeat, and channel-health subsystems at the very end via `setState` — after the channel-restart deferral loop. This fix delays the runtime config commit so it happens atomically with the subsystem publish:

1. `onHotReload` now uses `activate: false` (prepare only, no commit) when calling `activateRuntimeSecrets`.
2. A new `onBeforePublish` callback is passed to `applyHotReload`, which activates the prepared snapshot immediately before `setState` publishes the updated hooks, cron, heartbeat, and health-monitor references.
3. `sharedGatewaySessionGeneration` updates (auth client disconnect) are also deferred to after `applyHotReload` succeeds, avoiding unnecessary rollback on failure.
4. Error recovery is preserved: if `applyHotReload` fails after `onBeforePublish` has already committed the new config, the catch block rolls back via `activateSecretsRuntimeSnapshot(previousSnapshot)` and restores the context window cache.

The `server.impl.ts` needs no modification — the default `activatePreparedSnapshot` implementation uses the existing internal lazy loader for `activateSecretsRuntimeSnapshot`.

The `onNoopConfigCommit` path (no-op reloads) and `onRestart` path are unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators running busy gateways with hooks and cron will see consistent behavior during a config hot reload: hook routing, cron job lifecycle, and `getRuntimeConfig()` readers all observe either the old or the new configuration together, never a mix. This eliminates silent hook misrouting and lost cron jobs that could occur during deferred channel restarts.

## Evidence

**Tests:**
```
✓ src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts — 58 passed (including new test)
✓ src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts — 348 passed
✓ TypeScript (tsc --noEmit) — clean
✓ oxlint — 0 warnings, 0 errors
```

**New test:** `defers runtime config activation until after channel reload deferral when combined with hooks and cron` — sets active work to block the channel restart deferral, then verifies that `activatePreparedSnapshot` (runtime config commit) and `setState` (subsystem publish) are both NOT called while the deferral is active, and both ARE called atomically after the work drains.

**Error recovery:** Existing test `resets context metadata after a managed hot reload rolls back` continues to pass, confirming the catch block correctly restores the previous runtime snapshot and refreshes the context window cache when `applyHotReload` fails after the config was committed.

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.body:
## Summary

Implements #103387.

The Chrome transport scrapes Meet captions into an in-page buffer capped at 50 lines, and `status` exposed only the last 5 as `recentTranscript` — so for any real meeting the transcript was mostly discarded, and observe-mode users had to build fragile external pollers that still lose lines during fast speech. This follows the accumulation design proposed in the issue.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome.ts`: the status script now also ships its full in-page buffer as `transcriptWindow` (≤50 lines); `recentTranscript` stays at 5 lines for compatibility.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: the gateway merges `transcriptWindow` into a durable per-session transcript on every health refresh (join + status/health polls), deduped by the page-recorded `at`/`speaker`/`text` key, capped at the most recent **2000 lines** (fixed constant — no new config surface per the repo's config bar; `droppedLines` reports trimming). The window is merge input only and is stripped before health lands in status payloads, so `status` responses stay the same size. New `transcript(sessionId, { sinceIndex? })` refreshes browser health for active sessions and returns lines with absolute indices: `nextIndex` from one call is the `sinceIndex` for the next, which fixes the issue's "poll gap" problem exactly.
- `extensions/google-meet/index.ts`: new `googlemeet.transcript` gateway method and `transcript` tool action with optional `sinceIndex`.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts`: `openclaw googlemeet transcript <session-id> [--since <index>] [--json]`.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: observe-only section + tool action table updated.

Not included (flagged in the issue as optional): `chrome.transcriptFile` persistence — repo storage policy points that at SQLite rather than a JSONL sidecar, which is a separate product decision.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 207 tests passed. New regressions: overlapping page windows across polls accumulate without duplicates and the `sinceIndex` cursor returns exactly zero new lines at `nextIndex`; the cap test proves 2100 merged lines yield `droppedLines: 100`, retained lines 100..2099 in order (this test caught and fixed a dedupe-eviction bug during development); status payload health carries no `transcriptWindow`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, oxlint — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: caption lines beyond a 5-line window over a 50-line page buffer were irrecoverable; no way to retrieve a meeting transcript after the fact.
Real environment tested: the plugin's real join/status/transcript gateway methods driven through the existing stubbed browser-proxy harness, with the page status script's real JSON contract (including the new `transcriptWindow`) exercised end to end.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet`
Evidence after fix: joining with page windows `[1..3]` then polling with `[2..5]` yields transcript lines 1..5 exactly once with `nextIndex: 5`; `sinceIndex: 5` returns no lines; a 2100-line window yields `droppedLines: 100` with lines 100..2099 retained in order.
Observed result after fix: 207/207 tests pass; the transcript survives beyond the page window and is retrievable incrementally via CLI, gateway method, and tool action.
What was not tested: a live Google Meet call with real captions; the merge consumes the same parsed status payload shape the live path produces, and the page-side change is a one-line widening of what the existing scraper already records.

target.title: fix(mac-gateway): write launchd stderr to a log file and surface it in diagnostics (#90711)
target.body:
## Summary

The macOS LaunchAgent plist hard-coded `StandardErrorPath` to `/dev/null`, so a
gateway that crashed on a thrown startup error (e.g. `refusing to bind gateway …
without auth`, `failed to bind gateway socket …`) left **no trace on disk** —
operators saw a dead service with nothing to diagnose (issue #90711).

This routes launchd stderr to the resolved `gateway.err.log` for both fresh
installs and restart-rewrites, and then aligns OpenClaw's own macOS diagnostics
with that new logging contract.

## What changed since the first revision

The first revision only flipped the plist `StandardErrorPath`. As the review
noted, that left a real stderr file that OpenClaw's status tooling still treated
as suppressed. This revision fixes that mismatch:

- **`readLastGatewayErrorLine`** now reads the launchd supervisor stderr on
  darwin (it's the strongest failure signal, matching systemd/schtasks), so
  `openclaw gateway status`, `status --all`, doctor, and onboarding surface the
  real startup error instead of only stdout.
- **`gateway status`** and the daemon runtime-log hints print the
  `gateway.err.log` path instead of `Errors: suppressed`.

The stale "launchd supervisor combines child stderr into stdout" comment is
removed — the plist routes `StandardOutPath`/`StandardErrorPath` separately (no
`2>&1` merge), so stderr is a genuine, separate signal.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/diagnostics.test.ts src/daemon/runtime-hints.test.ts src/daemon/runtime-hints.windows-paths.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts` → all pass (updated for the new behavior).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts src/commands/doctor-gateway-daemon-flow.test.ts` → pass (downstream consumers of `readLastGatewayErrorLine`).
- `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean on changed files. Rebased onto current `main`.

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** launchd stderr is captured to `gateway.err.log`, and
  macOS status/diagnostics surface it instead of reporting it as suppressed.
- **Real environment tested:** local Vitest (daemon + CLI status suites).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** the Vitest commands above.
- **Evidence after fix:** updated tests assert the stderr path appears in the
  status output and that `readLastGatewayErrorLine` returns the launchd stderr
  error line on darwin.
- **What was not tested:** an end-to-end install/crash on a real macOS host

target.title: fix(mcp): stop ignored disabled servers from starting
target.body:
Closes #103954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could set `disabled: true` on an MCP server, see the config accepted without warning, and still have OpenClaw start that server process.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now reports the ineffective `disabled` key with actionable `enabled: false` guidance. `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates boolean `disabled` values to the inverse canonical `enabled` value, preserving an explicitly configured canonical value when both fields exist. The repair follows supported single-file `$include` ownership and continues to fail closed for root, array, nested, or sibling-override include layouts. Runtime consumers remain on the single `enabled` contract; no compatibility alias was added to steady-state startup code.

## User Impact

Operators with the reported config get a clear validation error instead of a silently ignored setting. Running `openclaw doctor --fix` repairs existing root files and supported single-file includes, after which disabled MCP servers are excluded from runtime startup.

## Evidence

Real on-disk include proof used an `openclaw.json5` root containing `mcp: { $include: "./mcp.json5" }`. The included file defined a disabled stdio server whose command would create a marker file if launched. The proof ran the production snapshot resolver, doctor migration, include-aware config writer, and session MCP runtime catalog (the process-launch boundary):

```text
{"doctorWrite":"single-file include preserved","migrated":{"enabled":false,"command":"/bin/sh","args":["-c","touch /private/tmp/openclaw-103970-proof/mcp-started; sleep 30"]},"runtimeServers":[],"processMarker":"absent"}
```

Post-proof filesystem assertions:

```text
root openclaw.json5: still contains only mcp.$include; no disabledProof server was flattened into root
included mcp.json5: contains "enabled": false; no "disabled" key remains
runtime catalog: zero configured MCP servers
process marker: absent
```

Focused and caller validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/config/mutate.test.ts \
  src/config/schema.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/config-flow-steps.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.test.ts \
  src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli.test.ts -- --reporter=dot

5 routed Vitest shards passed:
- config mutation: 128 tests
- doctor health persistence: 91 tests
- schema + legacy migration: 99 tests
- update CLI: 181 tests
- doctor config flow: 11 tests
- total: 510 tests

After the first exact-head CI run exposed one TypeScript indexing error and two stale exact-result assertions, the corrected final head reran the affected suites:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/invalid-plugin-config.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/config-flow-steps.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.test.ts \
  src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts -- --reporter=dot

3 routed Vitest shards passed; 276 tests passed

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit --pretty false
passed

node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8
core, extensions, and scripts shards passed
```

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <seven touched TypeScript files>
0 errors

oxfmt <eight touched files>
clean

git diff --check
clean
```

Fresh autoreview reported no accepted or actionable findings. Blacksmith Testbox could not be allocated because the `blacksmith` CLI is unavailable on this host; the narrow bundled-Node fallback and direct on-disk production-boundary proof above were used instead.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the schema, migration precedence, include write ownership, runtime exclusion path, and tests in this change.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): gate implicit discovery on AWS creds presence (#67288)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #67288. The `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin ran implicit Mantle provider discovery on every catalog refresh even when the user had no AWS credentials configured, emitting `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` log lines on every request and attempting IAM bearer-token generation through `@aws/bedrock-token-generator` that was guaranteed to fail. The user-visible symptom is constant log noise on Raspberry Pi installs with no AWS env vars set.

The sibling `amazon-bedrock` plugin already has the gate: at `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts:596`, implicit discovery short-circuits when `discovery.enabled !== true && !hasAwsCreds`. The mantle plugin had the `enabled === false` check but never the no-creds skip path.

## Fix

Mirror amazon-bedrock's gate in `resolveImplicitMantleProvider`:

```ts
const enabled = params.pluginConfig?.discovery?.enabled;
if (enabled === false) return null;
if (enabled !== true && !explicitBearerToken && !hasAwsSdkCreds(env)) return null;
```

Adds a small `hasAwsSdkCreds` helper that delegates to `resolveAwsSdkEnvVarName` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-runtime` (same helper bedrock uses via `resolveBedrockConfigApiKey`). Also exports `MantleDiscoveryConfig` so the type is consumable from the registration site.

## Boundary

- Extension-local fix (`extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/`); no core or schema changes.
- No new config keys. Users who explicitly set `plugins.entries.amazon-bedrock-mantle.config.discovery.enabled: true` still get implicit discovery (and the IAM token generation attempt) even without AWS creds — opt-in for cases where the bearer token is sourced through some out-of-band mechanism.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Users running OpenClaw on hosts with no AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi, default Docker installs) reported continuous `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` log lines on every request. The mantle plugin's `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` would attempt `generateBearerTokenFromIam(...)` even when neither `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` nor SDK creds were available, with the failed lookup logged on every catalog refresh. The amazon-bedrock plugin has a discovery.enabled gate plus a no-creds skip path; mantle was missing the no-creds skip.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `995ed29231` on Node 22 / Darwin 25.2.0, exercising the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider(...)` (`extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.ts`) against a real `process.env` shape (empty, with no AWS creds) and against the SDK-creds-aware `resolveAwsSdkEnvVarName` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-runtime`. No mocks of the resolver under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts` from the repository root, compiling the production source via tsgo and driving the live `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` against (a) empty env (no AWS creds) and (b) explicit `pluginConfig.discovery.enabled: false` with AWS bearer token set.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured terminal output from the `pnpm` invocation above on this exact branch:

  ```
   RUN  v4.1.6 /Users/shubh-trips/Documents/personal-project/open-source/openclaw

   ✓ |extension-providers| skips implicit discovery entirely when no AWS creds are present (#67288)
   ✓ |extension-providers| honors pluginConfig.discovery.enabled=false even when AWS creds are present (#67288)

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  29 passed (29)
     Duration  1.14s

  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.58s
  ```

  Runtime assertions captured by the live resolver runs: (a) with empty env (no `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, no SDK creds env), the resolver returns `null` AND the `tokenProviderFactory` spy is NOT called — proving we short-circuit before IAM token generation; (b) with `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` and `AWS_REGION` set but `pluginConfig.discovery.enabled: false`, the resolver still returns `null` and the token factory is not invoked — proving the explicit-disable path wins over creds presence; (c) the 27 existing discovery tests all continue to pass, including the previously-passing "returns null when no auth is available" case (the old behavior path that the user complained about — now it returns null *without* the noisy log).
- **Observed result after fix:** Installs without AWS credentials no longer see the per-request "Mantle IAM token generation unavailable" log lines and no longer attempt IAM bearer-token generation. The behavior for installs with `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` set or with full SDK creds is unchanged. The behavior for explicit `discovery.enabled: false` is unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** End-to-end behavior on an actual ARM64 Raspberry Pi (the bug's reported environment) — the regression test exercises the contract layer that the per-request catalog refresh consumes, which is what produced the user-visible log spam. Downstream catalog/registration flow is unchanged.

## Risk

- **Surface:** one bundled extension (`amazon-bedrock-mantle`), discovery-only gate.
- **Backwards compat:** installs that depend on implicit Mantle discovery without AWS creds env vars need to opt in via `plugins.entries.amazon-bedrock-mantle.config.discovery.enabled: true`. The original bug report explicitly disabled mantle to work around the noise, so the documented expected migration is: either set the bearer token / SDK creds, OR set `discovery.enabled: true` to opt in to the legacy noisy behavior.

## Closes

Fixes #67288

target.body:
Closes #103694

AI-assisted contribution.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using remote MCP servers would see repeated WARN-level startup noise when a tool schema used an informational, non-standard JSON Schema `format` such as `google-duration`.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now strips only unknown schema `format` values before non-draft MCP schemas reach the SDK AJV validator. target.title: fix(usage): reclaim refresh locks leaked by the current process (#103910)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost` can get stuck with `cacheStatus.status: "refreshing"` indefinitely: `pendingFiles` never drain, `refreshedAt` goes stale, and repeated queries hours apart return byte-identical responses frozen at an old `updatedAt`. Root cause: usage-cost refreshes serialize on a pid-stamped lock file (`.usage-cost-cache.json.lock`) whose staleness check trusts **pid-liveness alone** (`isUsageCostCacheRefreshRunning` → `isProcessRunning(lock.pid)`). A lock leaked by the gateway's **own process** — e.g. an in-process SIGUSR1 restart abandoning a mid-refresh promise before its `finally` releases, exactly the long-lived systemd deployment in the report — holds a pid that stays alive for the process's whole lifetime, so every subsequent `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath` returns `"busy"` forever while the background queue keeps re-scheduling. Fixes #103910.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track lock tokens held by this process in a module-level in-memory set: `acquire` registers the token, `release` removes it. The staleness check now reclaims a lock stamped with **our own pid whose token has no live in-process holder** (including tokenless legacy locks) — that lock cannot represent a running refresh in this process. Cross-process locks keep the existing pid-liveness semantics unchanged; genuinely running refreshes (registered token) are still respected. No new options or public surface.

## User Impact

`usage-cost` recovers by itself after a leaked lock instead of serving an aging snapshot that permanently claims to be "refreshing" — the failure mode that let a $1k+/month spend go unnoticed in the linked reports.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression test — forge a lock with `pid: process.pid` and an unregistered token (the leaked-self-lock state), then request a refresh:

```
main:     AssertionError: expected 'busy' to be 'refreshed'   ← stuck forever
this PR:  70/70 passed — lock reclaimed, refresh proceeds
```

The pre-existing "respects live usage cache locks even when they are old" test was retargeted to a genuinely foreign live pid (`process.ppid`), preserving its original intent under the new same-pid contract. Full suite `session-cost-usage.test.ts` 70/70; `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect Gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR adds those management paths while keeping ClawHub identity resolution, trust evaluation, and final installation enforcement on the Gateway.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable through `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install through `skills.search`, `skills.detail`, and `skills.install`.
- Add a fail-closed Android pre-install review dialog showing the resolved skill identity, exact version, publisher, ClawHub audit result, findings, and audit URL.
- Add the dedicated admin-scoped `skills.securityReview` RPC for one exact ClawHub release.
- Preserve final Gateway trust enforcement: Android can acknowledge a non-blocked review-required release only from the review dialog; a malicious/blocked release cannot expose an install action and remains rejected by `skills.install`.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android status and update the Android README/i18n inventory.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android mirrors the relevant workflows: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Contract

`skills.securityReview` is a separate `operator.admin` RPC. It is not an `items[]` extension to `skills.securityVerdicts`.

- Request: one required `slug`, one required exact `version`, and optional `ownerHandle`; additional properties are rejected.
- Registry boundary: the Gateway resolves the configured default ClawHub registry. The client cannot provide an arbitrary registry URL.
- Lookup scope: the handler requests only that exact release and does not scan installed skills.
- Identity binding: the returned requested slug/version and resolved slug/version must all match. When `ownerHandle` is supplied, the returned publisher must also match.
- Response: the existing sanitized `openclaw.skills.security-verdicts.v1` envelope with one reviewed item, including the derived `disposition` used by Android.
- Failure behavior: missing, unavailable, or identity-mismatched verdicts fail the RPC. Android treats a missing/invalid review as unavailable and keeps installation disabled.
- Final enforcement: `skills.install` independently re-evaluates Gateway trust policy. The pre-install review does not authorize or bypass installation.

`skills.securityVerdicts` remains the passive installed-skill verdict collection method and is unchanged by this contract.

target.title: Draft: add commands list and inspect inventory
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only operator/developer command inventory:

```text
openclaw commands list [--json|--markdown] [--plugin-descriptors]
openclaw commands inspect <command-path...> [--json|--markdown] [--plugin-descriptors]
```

This is the recommended initial implementation from [Command Catalog RFC #32](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/32). It joins command information OpenClaw already owns so compliance, diagnostics, documentation, policy tooling, and future scoped prompt consumers do not each rebuild the same registry joins.

## Scope

`commands list` joins existing command-owned sources:

- static CLI descriptors
- command routes and routed operations
- the current Commander tree
- opt-in plugin CLI descriptors
- caller-supplied node command declarations

`commands inspect` hydrates the requested lazy core/sub-CLI group, resolves runtime aliases, and joins exact command records with inherited route and routed-operation metadata.

This draft does not add ownerless tool adapters, aggregate audit/test/summary commands, prompt generation, generated docs, or a new execution path. Node records are supported in the object model but no live `node.list` / `node.describe` bridge is claimed yet.

## Plugin contract and failure behavior

Plugin descriptors may optionally report `effectProfile`, `commandExposure`, and `hidden`. Their values, defaults, and non-enforcement semantics are documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview.md` with an external-plugin example.

When `--plugin-descriptors` is requested, loader exceptions or error-level plugin diagnostics now fail the command. They cannot produce an apparently valid incomplete inventory. Warnings remain visible without invalidating successful results.

## Existing Gateway surface

OpenClaw already has Gateway RPC `commands.list` for agent-facing chat/native/skill/plugin commands. This CLI adds an operator/developer inventory; it does not replace or change the Gateway RPC. Future convergence remains an explicit RFC decision.

## Review layers

- [PR1: commands list](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/24)
- [PR2: commands inspect and ClawSweeper hardening](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/25)
- [Optional PR3: scoped prompt projection](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/26)

## Real behavior proof

Exact head: `90a7b1ca2b`

Core-only inventory, using an isolated state directory:

```text
schemaVersion=1
commandDescriptors=61
runtimeCommands=26
pluginCommands=0
```

Opt-in plugin inventory, also isolated:

```json

```

Controlled plugin registration failure:

```json
{"exitCode":1,"stdoutBytes":0,"errorMatched":true}
```

The failure fixture throws during plugin registration. The command emits no JSON document and exits nonzero with `Failed to load plugin CLI descriptor metadata` on stderr.

## Validation

- 44 focused inventory tests from the promoted PR1+PR2 stack
- latest hardening rerun: 10 focused CLI/metadata tests passed
- source execution proved core-only, plugin-enabled, and plugin-failure paths
- `git diff --check`
- clean final Codex review after the ClawSweeper fixes

The full local core TypeScript runner did not complete within two five-minute attempts on this worktree; it emitted no diagnostics. Focused Vitest compilation and runtime source execution passed.

## Feedback requested

Is `openclaw commands` the right initial public surface, with broader consumers added only after the command inventory contract is accepted?

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
